Privacy Policy

Updated: September 20, 2026


Use Your Own Node When Privacy Matters

dash.tx.taxi displays public Dash chain and mempool data through the backend configured by the site operator. For independent verification and the strongest network privacy, use your own Dash node and explorer.


Request Data

Normal website and API requests can reveal standard web metadata to the operator, including your IP address, user agent, requested URL, and request time. Server logs may be retained for reliability, abuse prevention, and debugging.


Local Preferences

Display preferences such as theme, denomination, fiat currency, language, and timezone may be stored in your browser. dash.tx.taxi does not require an account for ordinary explorer use.


Public Blockchain Data

Dash transactions, addresses, scripts, and blocks are public. Looking up an address or transaction can associate that lookup with your network metadata. Do not treat a public explorer as a privacy boundary.


External Links

This site links to tx.taxi contact channels, Dash documentation, and upstream source code. Those external services have their own privacy policies.


Open Source Attribution

Mempool names, logos, and trademarks remain the property of their respective owners; dash.tx.taxi is not affiliated with or endorsed by Mempool Holdings S.A. de C.V.

Terms of Service

Updated: September 20, 2026


Informational Explorer

dash.tx.taxi provides a view of public Dash blocks, transactions, addresses, mining data, fee estimates, and mempool state. It is an informational service, not a wallet, exchange, custodian, payment processor, or transaction-priority service.


No Control Over Dash Transactions

The operator cannot reverse, cancel, accelerate, recover, or redirect a Dash transaction. For wallet, exchange, or payment issues, contact the service that created or received the transaction.


Data and Availability

Explorer data may be delayed, incomplete, unavailable, or different from another node's view. Fee estimates are estimates only and do not guarantee confirmation. The service is provided as-is without a promise of uninterrupted availability or fitness for a particular purpose.


Acceptable Use

Do not abuse the website or API, interfere with service operation, bypass reasonable rate limits, or use the service unlawfully. Access may be limited when necessary to protect availability.


External Services

This site may link to tx.taxi contact channels, Dash references, upstream source code, and infrastructure dependencies. External websites have their own terms and policies.


Open Source

pages.label: Dash explorer guide
pages.title: Dash explorer guide - dash.tx.taxi
pages.description: Dash explorer coverage, amounts, fees, confirmations and data limits.
pages.html:
What this explorer covers

Search a Dash block height or hash, transaction ID, transparent Dash address, or a supported explorer URL. A 64-character hash can be a block or a transaction, so the search flow keeps a manual chain choice when a result is not uniquely confirmed.

Denomination1 DASH = 100,000,000 duffs
Fee displayduff/B
Target block intervalabout 2.5 minutes

Confirmations, InstantSend, and ChainLocks

A confirmation means the transaction is included in a block. Dash targets roughly one block every 2.5 minutes; actual intervals vary. The explorer’s pending list is an observed notification sample, so it does not estimate a confirmation time.

InstantSend is a Dash protocol that can lock eligible transactions through quorum consensus before block confirmation. ChainLocks are quorum signatures for blocks that protect the accepted chain against reorganizations. These are protocol concepts: this public API does not expose an authoritative InstantSend or ChainLock status endpoint. Where a transaction page shows an InstantSend label, it is a provider observation, not a substitute for wallet verification.

Data coverage and limits

Blocks, transactions, address balances, and indexed history come from the Dash Insight service. Address history is cursor-paginated in pages of 25. Transaction values and fees are integer duffs; fees are byte-based because Dash does not use a SegWit weight discount.

The pending panel only includes transactions observed from the provider notification stream after this explorer connected. It is intentionally not represented as the network-wide mempool. Fiat values are current USD observations, not historical prices. Provider failures return 503; a missing entity returns 404.

Dash special transactions

Dash Core supports special transactions, including masternode and quorum-related records and Platform withdrawals. A Platform withdrawal can carry its fee in the special payload, so calculating input value minus output value is not reliable for every special transaction. This explorer reads the documented payload fee when it is available and otherwise leaves the fee unavailable.

Protocol references

Dash Core features describes InstantSend and ChainLocks. Dash Core transaction reference covers transaction formats and special transaction data.
pages.markdown:
# Dash explorer guide

Canonical: https://dash.tx.taxi/docs/faq

## What this explorer covers

Search a Dash block height or hash, transaction ID, transparent Dash address, or a supported explorer URL. A 64-character hash can be a block or a transaction, so the search flow keeps a manual chain choice when a result is not uniquely confirmed.

Denomination | 1 DASH = 100,000,000 duffs |

Fee display | duff/B |

Target block interval | about 2.5 minutes |

## Confirmations, InstantSend, and ChainLocks

A confirmation means the transaction is included in a block. Dash targets roughly one block every 2.5 minutes; actual intervals vary. The explorer’s pending list is an observed notification sample, so it does not estimate a confirmation time.

InstantSend is a Dash protocol that can lock eligible transactions through quorum consensus before block confirmation. ChainLocks are quorum signatures for blocks that protect the accepted chain against reorganizations. These are protocol concepts: this public API does not expose an authoritative InstantSend or ChainLock status endpoint. Where a transaction page shows an InstantSend label, it is a provider observation, not a substitute for wallet verification.

## Data coverage and limits

Blocks, transactions, address balances, and indexed history come from the Dash Insight service. Address history is cursor-paginated in pages of 25. Transaction values and fees are integer duffs; fees are byte-based because Dash does not use a SegWit weight discount.

The pending panel only includes transactions observed from the provider notification stream after this explorer connected. It is intentionally not represented as the network-wide mempool. Fiat values are current USD observations, not historical prices. Provider failures return `503`; a missing entity returns `404`.

## Dash special transactions

Dash Core supports special transactions, including masternode and quorum-related records and Platform withdrawals. A Platform withdrawal can carry its fee in the special payload, so calculating input value minus output value is not reliable for every special transaction. This explorer reads the documented payload fee when it is available and otherwise leaves the fee unavailable.

## Protocol references

[Dash Core features](https://docs.dash.org/projects/core/en/stable/docs/explanations/features.html) describes InstantSend and ChainLocks. [Dash Core transaction reference](https://docs.dash.org/projects/core/en/stable/docs/reference/transactions.html) covers transaction formats and special transaction data.

pages.html:
REST API

The API is available on the same origin at https://dash.tx.taxi/api. It is read-only: it does not broadcast transactions, accept packages, or provide Electrum, Lightning, RBF, or enterprise endpoints.

Responses include X-DASH-Source, X-DASH-Observed-At, and X-DASH-Stale headers. Treat an observation timestamp as freshness information, not a blockchain timestamp.

Blocks

Get the current tip

GET /api/blocks/tip/height
curl https://dash.tx.taxi/api/blocks/tip/height

Get a block hash from a height

GET /api/block-height/:height
curl https://dash.tx.taxi/api/block-height/100000

Get block data and transactions

GET /api/v1/block/:hash
GET /api/block/:hash/txs/:startIndex

Use /api/block/:hash/txids for transaction IDs and /api/v1/block/:hash/summary for a bounded complete summary. A summary above 500 transactions reports unavailable instead of returning a partial result as complete.

curl https://dash.tx.taxi/api/v1/block/00000000000fd08c2fb661d2fcb0d49abb3a91e5f27082ce64feed3b4dede2e2

Transactions

Get a transaction

GET /api/tx/:txid

Values, fees, and output amounts are integer duffs. Optional suffixes are /status, /hex, and /outspends.

curl https://dash.tx.taxi/api/tx/836f0f697b6d3a6283c7c264a5a144c893e7b077ef4aea87dbb4f32d81ac86c5

Get outspends for several transactions

GET /api/txs/outspends?txids=:commaSeparatedTxids

The gateway accepts at most 25 transaction IDs in this batch.

Addresses and indexed history

Get an address summary

GET /api/address/:address

The returned confirmed and unconfirmed totals are in duffs. UTXO counts are unavailable from this provider and are returned as null.

curl https://dash.tx.taxi/api/address/XrgrCXZFhLNfyR4UKv9YT19CK7YVEPrc8Y

Page through address transactions

GET /api/address/:address/txs
GET /api/address/:address/txs/chain/:lastTxid

Each page has up to 25 indexed transactions. A cursor that has expired or no longer matches provider history is an error, rather than silently restarting at the first page.

Observed live data

Recent notification sample

GET /api/mempool/recent

Returns up to 100 pending transactions observed since the latest notification connection. It returns 503 while the provider notification stream is unavailable.

Snapshots, prices, and health

GET /api/v1/init-data
GET /api/v1/prices
GET /api/provider-health

Prices are current USD observations. Health describes gateway and provider freshness; it does not attest to transaction finality. The service does not provide a recommended-fee endpoint; use the observed transaction fee rates shown in the explorer without treating them as a confirmation forecast.

# Dash REST API

Canonical: https://dash.tx.taxi/docs/api/rest

## REST API

The API is available on the same origin at `https://dash.tx.taxi/api`. It is read-only: it does not broadcast transactions, accept packages, or provide Electrum, Lightning, RBF, or enterprise endpoints.

Responses include `X-DASH-Source`, `X-DASH-Observed-At`, and `X-DASH-Stale` headers. Treat an observation timestamp as freshness information, not a blockchain timestamp.

## Blocks

### Get the current tip

`GET` `/api/blocks/tip/height`

```
curl https://dash.tx.taxi/api/blocks/tip/height
```

### Get a block hash from a height

`GET` `/api/block-height/:height`

```
curl https://dash.tx.taxi/api/block-height/100000
```

### Get block data and transactions

`GET` `/api/v1/block/:hash`
`GET` `/api/block/:hash/txs/:startIndex`Use `/api/block/:hash/txids` for transaction IDs and `/api/v1/block/:hash/summary` for a bounded complete summary. A summary above 500 transactions reports unavailable instead of returning a partial result as complete.

```
curl https://dash.tx.taxi/api/v1/block/00000000000fd08c2fb661d2fcb0d49abb3a91e5f27082ce64feed3b4dede2e2
```

## Transactions

### Get a transaction

`GET` `/api/tx/:txid`Values, fees, and output amounts are integer duffs. Optional suffixes are `/status`, `/hex`, and `/outspends`.

```
curl https://dash.tx.taxi/api/tx/836f0f697b6d3a6283c7c264a5a144c893e7b077ef4aea87dbb4f32d81ac86c5
```

### Get outspends for several transactions

`GET` `/api/txs/outspends?txids=:commaSeparatedTxids`The gateway accepts at most 25 transaction IDs in this batch.

## Addresses and indexed history

### Get an address summary

`GET` `/api/address/:address`The returned confirmed and unconfirmed totals are in duffs. UTXO counts are unavailable from this provider and are returned as `null`.

```
curl https://dash.tx.taxi/api/address/XrgrCXZFhLNfyR4UKv9YT19CK7YVEPrc8Y
```

### Page through address transactions

`GET` `/api/address/:address/txs`
`GET` `/api/address/:address/txs/chain/:lastTxid`Each page has up to 25 indexed transactions. A cursor that has expired or no longer matches provider history is an error, rather than silently restarting at the first page.

## Observed live data

### Recent notification sample

`GET` `/api/mempool/recent`Returns up to 100 pending transactions observed since the latest notification connection. It returns `503` while the provider notification stream is unavailable.

### Snapshots, prices, and health

`GET` `/api/v1/init-data`
`GET` `/api/v1/prices`
`GET` `/api/provider-health`Prices are current USD observations. Health describes gateway and provider freshness; it does not attest to transaction finality. The service does not provide a recommended-fee endpoint; use the observed transaction fee rates shown in the explorer without treating them as a confirmation forecast.

pages.html:
WebSocket stream

Connect to wss://dash.tx.taxi/api/v1/ws. The explorer uses this stream for a bounded initial snapshot and subsequent Dash provider observations. It is not a general Dash Core RPC socket.

Connect

const socket = new WebSocket('wss://dash.tx.taxi/api/v1/ws');

socket.onmessage = event => console.log(event.data);

Reconnect with backoff after a close. A connection may initially report a snapshot or reconnecting state while upstream notifications are unavailable.

What the stream can contain

Messages may include the initial block snapshot, refreshed block data, observed pending transactions, and connection state. Observed pending transactions are bounded and are removed when later observations show them confirmed.

Do not derive a global mempool count, projected block template, InstantSend state, or ChainLock state from this stream.
pages.markdown:
# Dash WebSocket API

Canonical: https://dash.tx.taxi/docs/api/websocket

## WebSocket stream

Connect to `wss://dash.tx.taxi/api/v1/ws`. The explorer uses this stream for a bounded initial snapshot and subsequent Dash provider observations. It is not a general Dash Core RPC socket.

## Connect

```
const socket = new WebSocket('wss://dash.tx.taxi/api/v1/ws');

socket.onmessage = event => console.log(event.data);
```

Reconnect with backoff after a close. A connection may initially report a snapshot or reconnecting state while upstream notifications are unavailable.

## What the stream can contain

Messages may include the initial block snapshot, refreshed block data, observed pending transactions, and connection state. Observed pending transactions are bounded and are removed when later observations show them confirmed.

Do not derive a global mempool count, projected block template, InstantSend state, or ChainLock state from this stream.

## About dash.tx.taxi

## Dash

    Amounts are shown in DASH, duffs or your selected fiat currency. One DASH equals 100,000,000 duffs. Transaction sizes use bytes and fee rates use duff/B.

## Built on open source

        This explorer builds on the [Mempool Open Source Project](https://github.com/mempool/mempool). See [third-party attribution](https://dash.tx.taxi/3rdpartylicenses.txt) and contact the maintainer for source and license information.

# Privacy policy

Canonical: https://dash.tx.taxi/privacy-policy

## Privacy Policy

###### Updated: September 20, 2026

#### Use Your Own Node When Privacy Matters

      dash.tx.taxi displays public Dash chain and mempool data through the backend configured by the site operator. For independent verification and the strongest network privacy, use your own Dash node and explorer.

#### Request Data

      Normal website and API requests can reveal standard web metadata to the operator, including your IP address, user agent, requested URL, and request time. Server logs may be retained for reliability, abuse prevention, and debugging.

#### Local Preferences

      Display preferences such as theme, denomination, fiat currency, language, and timezone may be stored in your browser. dash.tx.taxi does not require an account for ordinary explorer use.

#### Public Blockchain Data

      Dash transactions, addresses, scripts, and blocks are public. Looking up an address or transaction can associate that lookup with your network metadata. Do not treat a public explorer as a privacy boundary.

#### External Links

      This site links to tx.taxi contact channels, Dash documentation, and upstream source code. Those external services have their own privacy policies.

#### Open Source Attribution

      Mempool names, logos, and trademarks remain the property of their respective owners; dash.tx.taxi is not affiliated with or endorsed by Mempool Holdings S.A. de C.V.

---

# Terms of service

Canonical: https://dash.tx.taxi/terms-of-service

## Terms of Service

###### Updated: September 20, 2026

#### Informational Explorer

      dash.tx.taxi provides a view of public Dash blocks, transactions, addresses, mining data, fee estimates, and mempool state. It is an informational service, not a wallet, exchange, custodian, payment processor, or transaction-priority service.

#### No Control Over Dash Transactions

      The operator cannot reverse, cancel, accelerate, recover, or redirect a Dash transaction. For wallet, exchange, or payment issues, contact the service that created or received the transaction.

#### Data and Availability

      Explorer data may be delayed, incomplete, unavailable, or different from another node's view. Fee estimates are estimates only and do not guarantee confirmation. The service is provided as-is without a promise of uninterrupted availability or fitness for a particular purpose.

#### Acceptable Use

      Do not abuse the website or API, interfere with service operation, bypass reasonable rate limits, or use the service unlawfully. Access may be limited when necessary to protect availability.

#### External Services

      This site may link to tx.taxi contact channels, Dash references, upstream source code, and infrastructure dependencies. External websites have their own terms and policies.

#### Open Source

      dash.tx.taxi is derived from [mempool/mempool](https://github.com/mempool/mempool). Contact [t.me/hiss](https://t.me/hiss) for the current reviewed fork source package.

---

# Dash explorer guide

Canonical: https://dash.tx.taxi/docs/faq

## What this explorer covers

Search a Dash block height or hash, transaction ID, transparent Dash address, or a supported explorer URL. A 64-character hash can be a block or a transaction, so the search flow keeps a manual chain choice when a result is not uniquely confirmed.

Denomination | 1 DASH = 100,000,000 duffs |

Fee display | duff/B |

Target block interval | about 2.5 minutes |

## Confirmations, InstantSend, and ChainLocks

A confirmation means the transaction is included in a block. Dash targets roughly one block every 2.5 minutes; actual intervals vary. The explorer’s pending list is an observed notification sample, so it does not estimate a confirmation time.

InstantSend is a Dash protocol that can lock eligible transactions through quorum consensus before block confirmation. ChainLocks are quorum signatures for blocks that protect the accepted chain against reorganizations. These are protocol concepts: this public API does not expose an authoritative InstantSend or ChainLock status endpoint. Where a transaction page shows an InstantSend label, it is a provider observation, not a substitute for wallet verification.

## Data coverage and limits

Blocks, transactions, address balances, and indexed history come from the Dash Insight service. Address history is cursor-paginated in pages of 25. Transaction values and fees are integer duffs; fees are byte-based because Dash does not use a SegWit weight discount.

The pending panel only includes transactions observed from the provider notification stream after this explorer connected. It is intentionally not represented as the network-wide mempool. Fiat values are current USD observations, not historical prices. Provider failures return `503`; a missing entity returns `404`.

## Dash special transactions

Dash Core supports special transactions, including masternode and quorum-related records and Platform withdrawals. A Platform withdrawal can carry its fee in the special payload, so calculating input value minus output value is not reliable for every special transaction. This explorer reads the documented payload fee when it is available and otherwise leaves the fee unavailable.

## Protocol references

[Dash Core features](https://docs.dash.org/projects/core/en/stable/docs/explanations/features.html) describes InstantSend and ChainLocks. [Dash Core transaction reference](https://docs.dash.org/projects/core/en/stable/docs/reference/transactions.html) covers transaction formats and special transaction data.

---

# Dash REST API

Canonical: https://dash.tx.taxi/docs/api/rest

## REST API

The API is available on the same origin at `https://dash.tx.taxi/api`. It is read-only: it does not broadcast transactions, accept packages, or provide Electrum, Lightning, RBF, or enterprise endpoints.

Responses include `X-DASH-Source`, `X-DASH-Observed-At`, and `X-DASH-Stale` headers. Treat an observation timestamp as freshness information, not a blockchain timestamp.

## Blocks

### Get the current tip

`GET` `/api/blocks/tip/height`

```
curl https://dash.tx.taxi/api/blocks/tip/height
```

### Get a block hash from a height

`GET` `/api/block-height/:height`

```
curl https://dash.tx.taxi/api/block-height/100000
```

### Get block data and transactions

`GET` `/api/v1/block/:hash`
`GET` `/api/block/:hash/txs/:startIndex`Use `/api/block/:hash/txids` for transaction IDs and `/api/v1/block/:hash/summary` for a bounded complete summary. A summary above 500 transactions reports unavailable instead of returning a partial result as complete.

```
curl https://dash.tx.taxi/api/v1/block/00000000000fd08c2fb661d2fcb0d49abb3a91e5f27082ce64feed3b4dede2e2
```

## Transactions

### Get a transaction

`GET` `/api/tx/:txid`Values, fees, and output amounts are integer duffs. Optional suffixes are `/status`, `/hex`, and `/outspends`.

```
curl https://dash.tx.taxi/api/tx/836f0f697b6d3a6283c7c264a5a144c893e7b077ef4aea87dbb4f32d81ac86c5
```

### Get outspends for several transactions

`GET` `/api/txs/outspends?txids=:commaSeparatedTxids`The gateway accepts at most 25 transaction IDs in this batch.

## Addresses and indexed history

### Get an address summary

`GET` `/api/address/:address`The returned confirmed and unconfirmed totals are in duffs. UTXO counts are unavailable from this provider and are returned as `null`.

```
curl https://dash.tx.taxi/api/address/XrgrCXZFhLNfyR4UKv9YT19CK7YVEPrc8Y
```

### Page through address transactions

`GET` `/api/address/:address/txs`
`GET` `/api/address/:address/txs/chain/:lastTxid`Each page has up to 25 indexed transactions. A cursor that has expired or no longer matches provider history is an error, rather than silently restarting at the first page.

## Observed live data

### Recent notification sample

`GET` `/api/mempool/recent`Returns up to 100 pending transactions observed since the latest notification connection. It returns `503` while the provider notification stream is unavailable.

### Snapshots, prices, and health

`GET` `/api/v1/init-data`
`GET` `/api/v1/prices`
`GET` `/api/provider-health`Prices are current USD observations. Health describes gateway and provider freshness; it does not attest to transaction finality. The service does not provide a recommended-fee endpoint; use the observed transaction fee rates shown in the explorer without treating them as a confirmation forecast.

---

# Dash WebSocket API

Canonical: https://dash.tx.taxi/docs/api/websocket

## WebSocket stream

Connect to `wss://dash.tx.taxi/api/v1/ws`. The explorer uses this stream for a bounded initial snapshot and subsequent Dash provider observations. It is not a general Dash Core RPC socket.

## Connect

```
const socket = new WebSocket('wss://dash.tx.taxi/api/v1/ws');

socket.onmessage = event => console.log(event.data);
```

Reconnect with backoff after a close. A connection may initially report a snapshot or reconnecting state while upstream notifications are unavailable.

## What the stream can contain

Messages may include the initial block snapshot, refreshed block data, observed pending transactions, and connection state. Observed pending transactions are bounded and are removed when later observations show them confirmed.

Do not derive a global mempool count, projected block template, InstantSend state, or ChainLock state from this stream.
